title: Discrete Sampling
primary_title: Spectral Independence and Local-to-Global Techniques for Optimal Mixing of Markov Chains
edition_note: arXiv submission v4 is dated September 16; downloaded PDF title page reads September 18, 2025. Use the version and byte fingerprint, not date alone.
scope: Finite/discrete state-space sampling, not numerical discretization of continuous-state Langevin dynamics.
formalization_status: scaffold; no discrete Lean theorem closure asserted

sections.title: Key Definitions: Spectral Independence and the Influence Matrix
Main Results: Fast Mixing via Spectral Independence

chapters.guide: Start with finite support and normalization, then audit the single-site conditional update. One update chooses one site; stationarity alone is not a mixing theorem. The binary hard-core example is not all spin systems.

chapters.title: Properties of the Influence Matrix

sections.title: Bounding Spectral Radius of Influence Matrix

chapters.guide: Reuse covariance, symmetric matrix and weighted-inner-product algebra. The displayed off-diagonal binary influence assumes both conditional events are feasible; frozen sites need removal or an explicit convention.

chapters.title: Markov Chain Fundamentals

sections.title: Mixing Time and Total Variation Distance
Mixing Time Bounds via Spectral Gap

chapters.guide: Pull this foundation forward before advanced spectral-independence proofs. Fix reversibility and whether the result concerns P^k or exp(t(P-I)); a positive relaxation gap is not an absolute-gap guarantee for a periodic discrete-time chain.

chapters.title: Rapid Mixing from Spectral Independence

sections.title: Local to Global: Random Walk Theorem of Alev-Lau
Local Walk Connection to Influence Matrix

chapters.guide: Uniform control must cover every feasible pinning required by the theorem, not just the unconditional law. Separate conditional support bookkeeping from spectral estimates.

chapters.title: Random Walk Theorem: Proof of Local-to-Global

sections.title: Inductive Proof of Random Walk Theorem: Proof of Theorem 4.1

chapters.guide: Use one canonical variance/Dirichlet/Rayleigh-quotient API and explicit up/down-walk adapters. The displayed variational formula assumes a finite reversible nontrivial chain.

chapters.title: Optimal Mixing Time for Glauber from Spectral Independence

sections.title: Fast Mixing of Uniform Block Dynamics
Optimal Relaxation Time of Glauber: Proof of Theorem 1.5
Improved Random Walk Theorem: Proof of Theorem 6.1
Proofs of Basic Facts for Dirichlet Form and Variance
Optimal Mixing Time via Entropy Decay

chapters.guide: Distinguish variance factorization, entropy factorization, log-Sobolev and modified log-Sobolev inequalities. The reference measure and clock determine constants; converting a relaxation bound into mixing needs its own theorem.

chapters.title: Matroids

sections.title: Main Theorem: Fast Mixing of Bases-Exchange Walk

chapters.guide: Use Mathlib matroid and finite-set primitives before defining a bases-exchange walk. The formula is the uniform target on a nonempty finite set of bases, not a mixing assertion.

chapters.title: Trickle-Down Theorem

sections.title: Rapid Mixing of Bases-Exchange Walk: Proof of Theorem 1.15
Connections to Spectral Independence and Log-Concavity
Proof of the Trickle-Down Theorem: Proof of Theorem 8.1

chapters.guide: Track links, local walks and pinning operators. Log-concavity of a generating polynomial is not the same predicate as log-concavity of a Euclidean density. The display is a proof-program orientation, not a theorem.

chapters.title: Methods for Establishing Spectral Independence
chapters.guide: Treat correlation decay, zero-freeness, coupling independence and relaxation-time methods as different sufficient routes. Specify model, degree, boundary conditions and all pinnings; one covariance calculation is insufficient.

chapters.title: Critical Point Analysis using the Field Dynamics

sections.title: SI implies Fast Mixing of Field Dynamics
Fast Mixing of Glauber Dynamics from Field Dynamics

chapters.guide: A field tilt changes the distribution. Record stationary laws and the comparison theorem separately; transporting a gap requires quantitative bounds, not a change of notation.

chapters.title: Random Regular Graphs via Field Dynamics

sections.title: Proof of the trickle-down for the field dynamics

chapters.guide: Random-regular-graph results have a probability-over-graphs contract. Keep that probability separate from sampler success and Markov-chain randomness; no worst-case general-graph claim follows.

chapters.title: Extensions to Other Spin Systems: Ising Model and Colorings

sections.title: Multispin Systems: Colorings and Edge Colorings

chapters.guide: The display is the finite, zero-field Ising target in the monograph convention. The factor exp(beta|E|) cancels on normalization. Section 12 states results without proofs: follow the cited original papers before claiming closure. Temperature, sign, degree, fields and boundary conditions cannot be dropped.

dependency_semantics: ASTIS planned prerequisite windows, not a dependency figure asserted by the source; chapter reading order is unchanged. Only theorem-level audited dependencies enter Lean Branches.

entry_windows.purpose: shared finite probability, conditional kernels, reversibility, variance and gap before advanced SI
early Ising target and clock conventions; defer cited mixing theorems to exact external proofs
conditional influence matrices with feasible pinnings
entropy factorization and mLSI after the shared entropy floor

source_issues.observation: The PDF prints X_(t+1)(w)=X_t(v) for w != v, while its following prose says the other spins stay fixed.
source_issues.rule: Do not silently edit a faithful source statement. Audit the corrected conditional-update contract and record source/Lean/reconstructed-text differences.

source_issues.observation: The monograph explicitly states that the results in this section are not proved here.
source_issues.rule: Pin each cited original result and exact hypothesis adapter before any corresponding formalization claim.

supporting_sources.title: Levin–Peres, with contributions by Wilmer: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed. (2017)
supporting_sources.use: Basic finite chains, coupling, spectral analysis and mixing-time lower bounds; not claimed to have an arXiv edition.

supporting_sources.title: Hugo Duminil-Copin: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice
supporting_sources.use: Ising/Potts equilibrium, finite/infinite volume and phase transitions. Not a replacement for a rapid-mixing proof.

supporting_sources.title: Blanca et al.: On Mixing of Markov Chains: Coupling, Spectral Independence, and Entropy Factorization
supporting_sources.use: Pin theorem/version for coupling-to-SI and entropy-factorization adapters; preserve all assumptions.

supporting_sources.title: Chen–Liu–Vigoda: Optimal Mixing of Glauber Dynamics: Entropy Factorization via High-Dimensional Expansion
supporting_sources.use: Source-specific entropy factorization and spin-system mixing proofs; audit cited statement, not just title.

supporting_sources.title: Jan Maas: Gradient flows of the entropy for finite Markov chains
supporting_sources.use: Finite reversible irreducible chains and a chain-dependent logarithmic-mean transport metric; not ordinary W2 on a finite set.
